== Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz ==

Eureka is a small kitten belonging to Dorothy, who carries her along in a basket that a fellow traveler at first mistakes for a cage of canary-birds. Dorothy explains that she named the kitten Eureka because she found it, recalling that Uncle Henry says the word means "I have found it."

While the group crosses the river in the Valley of Voe using magic leaves that let them walk on water, Eureka is at first dreadfully afraid of getting wet, but soon frisks along beside the buggy without fear. During the crossing she snaps up and eats a small fish that swims too close to the surface, prompting Dorothy to caution her to be careful what she eats in the enchanted valley. Eureka is also able to speak, and when the group can hear one another again she admits that being able to see again makes her dreadfully hungry, asking the Wizard's permission to eat one of the fat little piglets.

Later, in the Princess's palace, Dorothy's white kitten is seen slipping out through a closed door and running up the stairs shortly before one of the Princess's tiny piglets goes missing. The Princess concludes that her piglet has been eaten and declares that the offender must be punished, but Dorothy protests that she does not believe Eureka would do such a dreadful thing. When Dorothy calls for her, Eureka is found hiding under the bed.

* Ozma accuses Eureka and orders her imprisoned and put on trial for murder before a jury of nine.
* Wizard secretly gives Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet to produce as proof of Eureka's innocence if convicted.
* Jury finds Eureka guilty, but Tin Woodman produces the duplicate piglet, seemingly proving innocence.
* Eureka reveals the collar mismatch and confesses the real piglet fell into a vase, where it is found alive.

== Narrative role ==

Eureka is Dorothy's kitten, present when the group lands in the glass city of the Mangaboos, a vegetable people ruled by the Prince, where she and Jim unexpectedly gain the power of speech. The new Princess who takes power there spares Dorothy, [[Zeb]], and the Wizard, but condemns Jim, Eureka, and the piglets to be driven into the Black Pit within the mountain. Traveling on with the Wizard, Dorothy, Zeb, and Jim, Eureka escapes invisible bears in the Valley of Voe when the group rubs magic leaves on their feet to walk across the water.

Eureka later reveals a mismatch in a piglet's collar and confesses that the real piglet had fallen into a vase, where it is found alive. Ozma's white piglet then goes missing from her boudoir, and Dorothy's kitten Eureka is seen fleeing the room. Ozma accuses Eureka of the piglet's disappearance and orders her imprisoned and put on trial for murder before a jury of nine. Before the verdict, the Wizard secretly gives Tin Woodman a duplicate piglet to produce as proof of Eureka's innocence should she be convicted. The jury ultimately finds Eureka guilty, but Tin Woodman produces the duplicate piglet, seemingly proving her innocence.

== Personality ==

Eureka's most consistent trait is her appetite: confronted with easy prey — a fish in the river, the Wizard's tiny piglets — her first instinct is to eat it, and she voices this desire openly, at one point asking outright whether she may "eat just one of the fat little piglets." Hunger, for her, arrives together with the pleasure of simply being able to see again, suggesting a direct, unreflective link between appetite and satisfaction.

She is also adaptable and quick to recover from fear. Crossing the river in the Valley of Voe, she is at first "dreadfully afraid of getting wet," but once set down she abandons that fear entirely and trots alongside the buggy "without being scared a bit." This rapid shift from anxiety to playful ease suggests a kitten who, once a threat has passed, does not dwell on it.

Her boldness draws suspicion from others. When Princess Ozma's piglet disappears and the kitten is seen fleeing the scene, the household immediately assumes Eureka is guilty — a conclusion Dorothy, defending her, refuses to accept. Whatever the truth of that particular incident, the readiness of others to suspect her matches an earlier description of her as not always "well behaved."

== Appearance ==

Eureka is a white kitten kept by Dorothy, who carries her rather than a cage when traveling.

== Powers ==

Eureka's defining trait is an unexplained capacity for speech, unusual for a cat. During the crossing of the Valley of Voe she addresses the Wizard directly, telling him she can see again and asking, "Mr. Wizard, may I eat just one of the fat little piglets?" Beyond this ability to speak and reason, Eureka shows an ordinary hunting reflex, snatching a fish from the water and eating it "as quick as a wink" when the party crosses the enchanted river.

== Trivia ==

* The name "Eureka" comes from the exclamation meaning "I have found it"; Dorothy named her kitten this way, explaining that Uncle Henry had taught her the meaning of the word.
* Eureka is Dorothy's white kitten; when Zeb first heard her meowing and asked if it were canary-birds, Dorothy corrected him that it was only Eureka.
* While crossing the enchanted river in the Valley of Voe, Eureka was at first dreadfully afraid of getting wet but soon moved confidently alongside the buggy, catching and eating a small fish that swam too near the surface.
